text:
If you're looking for Alexander Kerfoot in Nashville's box scores, check the blocked shots. He has 22 of them in 20 games, more than his 16 shots on goal, on about 16 minutes a night for a team that has won seven straight. His scoring is light: 6 points, 2 of them goals, and just 2 points in his last ten games.

Our numbers had him around 4.2 points over that stretch, so a little of it is bad luck, but he isn't built to create. His own chances (0.36 expected goals per 60, a measure of chance quality) are down from 0.48 last season in Utah, and his ice time has slipped by more than a minute. What he brings is legs and defense. NHL EDGE has his top speed in the 98th percentile, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.11 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there last season (88th percentile), on a small sample of 435 minutes. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 60% of his shots coming off the rush. This season the Predators' share of five-on-five expected goals is slightly better with him on than off.
headline: Alexander Kerfoot's value lives off the scoresheet
